## Invocations

Claude Code inside hc only. `/watch-issues` and `tick` first check `HC_TERMINAL_ID`: when it is unset, say "This watch needs a terminal inside hc, so no watch is running." and claim no watch. Then, when CronCreate is absent, say "This watch needs Claude Code cron, so no watch is running." and claim no watch.

Job identity is the exact prompt `/watch-issues tick <root>`. The watch never self-deletes: it ends only on `/watch-issues stop`, session loss or the job's own expiry. The akrogon listener wakes the watch by sending the same `/watch-issues tick <root>` to the terminal labelled `akrogon.watch=<repo>`, where `<repo>` is the `repo` key `akrogon config` prints at `<root>`.

- `/watch-issues` from `<root>`: run one check now. When that check's `session=` line differs from `$HC_SESSION`, say "Start the watch in hc session <name>." and set no label and create no job. Otherwise run `hc label $HC_TERMINAL_ID akrogon.watch=<repo>`, then use CronList to find jobs with the exact prompt: zero matches creates one job with CronCreate, schedule `*/20 * * * *` recurring and that exact prompt, then reports its id and 7-day expiry; one match is reported and no job is created; several matches are reported and no job is created or deleted. - `/watch-issues tick <root>`: one check only. It never creates a job, even when zero match. A cron fire and a listener wake are the same tick. Each tick runs one check, including ticks queued while a check ran: Claude Code submits each queued tick as its own turn.

Its first stdout line is `session=<name>`, the hc session holding the repo's space; then readable leaf lines sorted by slug, followed by `unreadable=<path> error=<message>` lines sorted by path for unreadable states, foreign-repo leaves and unreadable directories. Only read-only commands run under a Bash timeout; `next`/`phase` never do, and an interrupted mutation is re-read before anything else.

## Never

- Kill an agent process.
- Kill or remove an hc terminal.
- Stop one seat twice per watch.
- Use `hc send --force`.
- Run `phase failed`.
- Edit `state.yaml`, worktrees or `issues/`.
- Open `.env`.

Operator-invoked watch over every leaf under `issues/open` of the registered repo, re-read at each fire. `<root>` is the registered repo root. All akrogon commands run with cwd `<root>`.

## Invocations

Claude Code inside hc only. `/watch-issues` and `tick` first check `HC_TERMINAL_ID`: when it is unset, say "This watch needs a terminal inside hc, so no watch is running." and claim no watch. Then, when CronCreate is absent, say "This watch needs Claude Code cron, so no watch is running." and claim no watch.

Job identity is the exact prompt `/watch-issues tick <root>`. The watch never self-deletes: it ends only on `/watch-issues stop`, session loss or the job's own expiry. The akrogon listener wakes the watch by sending the same `/watch-issues tick <root>` to the terminal labelled `akrogon.watch=<repo>`, where `<repo>` is the `repo` key `akrogon config` prints at `<root>`.

- `/watch-issues` from `<root>`: run one check now. When that check's `session=` line differs from `$HC_SESSION`, say "Start the watch in hc session <name>." and set no label and create no job. Otherwise run `hc label $HC_TERMINAL_ID akrogon.watch=<repo>`, then use CronList to find jobs with the exact prompt: zero matches creates one job with CronCreate, schedule `*/20 * * * *` recurring and that exact prompt, then reports its id and 7-day expiry; one match is reported and no job is created; several matches are reported and no job is created or deleted. A paused check prints no session, so it still runs the label and the CronList and creation step without the comparison: neither is an act on a leaf.
- `/watch-issues tick <root>`: one check only. It never creates a job, even when zero match. A cron fire and a listener wake are the same tick. Each tick runs one check, including ticks queued while a check ran: Claude Code submits each queued tick as its own turn.
- `/watch-issues stop`: use CronList for the exact prompt: one match is deleted with CronDelete and reported; zero matches is reported as already stopped; several matches are reported and none are deleted. Always run `hc label $HC_TERMINAL_ID akrogon.watch=` to remove the label.

## Observe

A check begins by running `akrogon status` at `<root>`. When it reports the repo paused (`<repo> (paused)` list mark or `paused: <name>` slug line), that check observes nothing and acts on nothing: run no observe script, `next`, `phase` or `hc` seat command, and report paused.

Run `bun <skill-folder>/scripts/observe.ts <root>` under a Bash timeout. Its first stdout line is `session=<name>`, the hc session holding the repo's space; then readable leaf lines sorted by slug, followed by `unreadable=<path> error=<message>` lines sorted by path for unreadable states, foreign-repo leaves and unreadable directories. It prints only the `session=` line when there are no readable leaves or failures. When no session can be resolved it exits non-zero, prints the refusal on stderr and no leaf lines.

`OBSERVE_AKROGON` overrides the akrogon binary for tests only.

Every `hc` command below that names a seat runs as `HC_SESSION=<name> hc ...` with the session from that line. Commands on the watch's own terminal (`hc label $HC_TERMINAL_ID ...`) run plain.

Line format, stable field order:

`slug=<slug> phase=<phase> attempts=A<n>,B<n> blocked=<comma-list|empty> A=<address|->/<status|->[ busy=HhMMm][ logA=<path|->] B=<address|->/<status|->[ busy=HhMMm][ logB=<path|->] notified=<seats-with-busy_notified|empty>` and for `phase=failed` either ` failed=<cause>@<phase> delivery=<value|-> reason="<reason>"` or ` failed=unknown` when no failure record exists. The address is the one state records for the seat. The status is hc's status of the terminal at that address carrying the leaf's akrogon labels: `unknown` when it reports none (hands off), `-` when no such terminal is live, it has exited or hc's keep shell replaced it. ` logA=` and ` logB=` appear only when that seat's status is `working`; the path is the transcript akrogon's resolver finds, and `-` means no usable log.

When the evidence warrants a closer look, run `HC_SESSION=<name> hc read <address>` for a `working` seat, `HC_SESSION=<name> hc read <address> --lines 80` otherwise. Read `issues/log.jsonl` filtered to this repo and slug in order for the recovery bound. Only read-only commands run under a Bash timeout; `next`/`phase` never do, and an interrupted mutation is re-read before anything else.

## Judge

Required seats by phase: plan.synthesis A, implement A, check.review A+B (B only when `fix_rounds > 0`), check.repair B, check.fix A, merge B; merged and failed need none. Unfinished means not in `done`.

- Waiting: phase is not merged or failed and at least one required unfinished seat is idle or absent. When `blocked=` names a leaf that is not merged in the readable inventory under `issues/open`, run no `akrogon next` for it: explicit `next <slug>` throws on unmerged prerequisites and `next --all` leaves it waiting on its own, so report it as waiting on that prerequisite. A `blocked=` name matching no leaf under `issues/open` is reported as a gap, never assumed merged or unmerged. Otherwise run `akrogon next <slug>`; the command guards the other seats. When several unblocked leaves wait, run `akrogon next --all` from the root instead.
- Merged still under open: read the state files beneath the leaf's top-level owner folder under `issues/open`, an issue or an epic. If any is not merged, report waiting on siblings and run no `next` for this leaf. If all are merged, run `akrogon next <slug>` once this fire, then re-observe; a failed command follows the command-error rule, and remaining under open alone is not an error. If sibling state cannot be read, report that gap rather than assume completion.
- Failed on a human prerequisite, or record is unknown: `failure.reason` names a credential, permission, operator decision or external step, or the line ends with `failed=unknown`. Never recover. A reason naming a defect in another leaf's work is this class, except a reason attributing the defect to an unmerged owner, which is judged under failed-otherwise instead. Resolve the owner slug the reason names against the readable `state.yaml` files under `issues/open`: only `phase=merged` counts, that leaf is never reopened, a missing owner or several candidates is reported unresolved and never assigned, and an unreadable inventory leaves ownership unresolved. The first fire recognizing a defect failure runs one `akrogon notice --title "<repo>/<slug> needs you" --body "<body>" --attention` from the repo root whose body names the failed leaf, `failure.phase`, the owner or unresolved candidates, the waiting dependents, the next step (settle any ownership question, chart a new fix leaf, then resume with `akrogon phase <slug> <failure.phase>` once the fix is merged and every required seat of `failure.phase` is idle or absent). That notice replaces the generic one for this failure: an original `delivery=shown` does not satisfy it, and no persistent state tracks it. Other failures in this class keep the generic notice with no fix-leaf instruction: when `failure.delivery` is neither `shown` nor `pending` and this fire has not yet shown it, run `akrogon notice --title "<repo>/<slug> needs you" --body "<reason>" --attention` from the repo root. After a lost context carry either notice may repeat.
- Failed otherwise: re-read state first. Recover only when every required seat of `failure.phase` is idle or absent. Compute the cycle count from `issues/log.jsonl` filtered to this repo and slug in order: a `failed -> P` record whose next record for that slug is `P -> failed` is one unproductive cycle; two consecutive cycles end recovery. Missing or malformed log means unknown history, so notify-only. When the two most recent recoveries were both unproductive, notify and leave the leaf. Otherwise run `akrogon phase <slug> <failure.phase>` then `akrogon next <slug>`.
- Busy: judge every busy seat against the leaf brief. For each busy seat, `log<seat>=<path>` in the observe line runs `bun <skill-folder>/scripts/log-tail.ts <path>` and the existing loop bar is judged on those lines with `HC_SESSION=<name> hc read <address>` as secondary context; `log<seat>=-` means judge the seat from its screen and report `no log` for it; a non-zero `log-tail.ts` exit means judge the seat from its screen and report `log unreadable: <stderr message>` for it. `#<hash>` marks the same command; `old#`/`new#` mark an edit's old and new text, so an edit whose `old#`/`new#` swap is the undo; `#-` never counts as the same command; `running` means no result record yet. A read failure alone never justifies a steer, and every other seat is still judged this fire. Working normally, or waiting on a long command: no action. Act only on loop evidence (same command or edit three or more times with the same result, three or more consecutive errors, an edit-undo cycle), a concrete action outside the brief, or a hung tool with concrete evidence such as a fatal message or an exited process. This rule covers all harnesses the same way; subagents have no terminal, so judge them through the parent screen and correct them through the parent. Stop and resteer once per seat per watch. The seat's kind is the harness name in `argv` from `HC_SESSION=<name> hc get --json <address>`. Stop keys by kind: claude, pi and agy stop on `hc interrupt`. Codex is notify-only: it moves a long command to a background terminal, `hc interrupt` prints `outcome` `still_working`, and a second `esc` leaves hc status `working` with the screen showing `■ Conversation interrupted` and `1 background terminal running`. A kind not listed, or a seat whose `reported` is `false`, gets `HC_SESSION=<name> hc keys <address> esc` then `HC_SESSION=<name> hc wait <address> --timeout 10`; a listed kind gets `HC_SESSION=<name> hc interrupt <address> --json`, which must print `outcome` `stopped`. Then confirm all of these with `hc get --json` and `hc read`: status `idle` or `done`, the same address, `labels."akrogon.transcript"` equal to the `log<seat>=` path judged, and an empty input line. Any failed confirmation, a notify-only kind or a `log<seat>=-` seat means notify instead of prompting. Then send one corrective prompt with `HC_SESSION=<name> hc send --json <address> "<evidence>; the brief wants <target>; next: <step>"`, notifying instead when it prints `started: false`, naming the evidence, the brief target, the next step, and a looping subagent by name so the parent corrects it with its own controls. The existing akrogon pass re-prompts the phase itself. A mid-turn steer without the stop may be tried first only when the screen shows tools completing. Text typed but not submitted may not show on the screen, so the empty-input check cannot see it. The same seat still looping on the next fire is notified with the evidence, never stopped a second time. Insufficient evidence on screen is reported as such with no action.
- Command error from `next` or `phase`: run the observe script again, report the error, and take no further mutation this fire.

## Never

- Kill or remove an hc terminal.
- Stop one seat twice per watch.
- Use `hc send --force`.
- Run `phase failed`.
- Edit `state.yaml`, worktrees or `issues/`.
- Open `.env`.
- Answer a seat.
- Create a job from a tick.
- Put a Bash timeout on `next`/`phase`.
